data.translation:
📉 BofA cut Nvidia's price target from $350 to $280

Bank of America (BofA) Global Research lowered its price target for Nvidia from $350 to $280 following Jensen Huang's departure as CEO.

This revision represents a 20% drop from the previous target.

Despite lowering its price target, the analyst team led by Vivek Arya maintained its previous “Buy” rating on Nvidia.

BofA had removed Nvidia from its “US 1” list of most preferred stocks on November 10.

Following Huang's resignation, the company's Chief Financial Officer, Colette Kress, is serving as interim CEO.

#Nvidia #BofA #NVDA #TeknolojiHisseleri

📉 BofA: Don't return to risky assets until oil falls below $70 and US Treasury yields fall below 4.5%

Bank of America strategist Michael Hartnett said risk-averse positions should be maintained until interest rate hikes end and financial conditions ease.

BofA expects US 10-year Treasury yields to fall below 4.5% in December or January, while the dollar is expected to peak in February or March.

The bank forecasts that the global interest rate hiking cycle will end no earlier than April 2027.

The optimistic scenario for the S&P 500 is above 8,000 points, while the pessimistic scenario is below 7,000 points.

According to Hartnett, falling oil prices, declining bond yields and a weakening dollar will be the key conditions for a return to risky assets.

#BofA #MichaelHartnett #SP500 #KüreselPiyasalar

result.text:
Three money stories are all over my feed this week, and they all come down to one question: who's actually getting ahead right now?

The October inflation report came in hot, and Bank of America now says a half-point rate hike in December could be on the table. That would make borrowing even more expensive.

Housing isn't any easier. Zillow counted a record 242 U.S. cities this year where a typical starter home costs $1 million or more, and for anyone buying now, higher mortgage rates mean bigger monthly payments on top of that.

Calling that a starter home is a stretch.

Then who is getting ahead? Right now, the money is chasing AI. Anthropic is targeting a fully diluted valuation of around $1.4 trillion, with trading reportedly expected to begin on Nov. 19 or 20.

I'm not sure about that valuation. But I use AI every day, and I want to see it keep getting better.

Expenses keep rising, but my income hasn't kept up, so I need to find ways to earn more. That's why I'm learning AI.

I don't expect it to pay off overnight. I'm just using it to get more done at work and explore different fields.

So I'd rather get on board now than watch AI pull away. I believe in the future, and I believe in AI.
